title: Marked stack formal objects and their versality
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] equipped with an $R$-algebra structure, and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F$ be a category over schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. When $F$ is fibred in groupoids, use the meaning of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For each commutative $R$-algebra $A$, write $F(A)$ for its fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For an $R$-map $a:A\to B$, an arrow over $a$ from $y\in F(B)$ to $x\in F(A)$ means an actual arrow $y\to x$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(a)$; in the fibred-in-groupoids case it gives the pullback identification. A complete marked local algebra is a Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], equipped with an $R$-algebra isomorphism $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix $x\in F(k)$. A marked formal object over $C$ at $x$ consists of $\eta_n\in F(C/\mathfrak m_C^{n+1})$ for $n\geq0$, arrows $\eta_n\to\eta_m$ over the quotient maps for every $n\leq m$, satisfying identity and composition, and arrows $x\to\eta_n$ over the specified residue maps, commuting with these transitions. For a local $R$-map $f:C\to A$ preserving the specified residue identification, where $A$ is Artinian local with specified residue field $k$, choose a positive power $\mathfrak m_C^{n+1}$ killed by $f$ and evaluate by pulling back $\eta_n$ along the induced quotient map. These evaluations are identified at every larger level by the transition arrows. The formal object is versal if, for every local residue-preserving surjection $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ between such Artinian local $R$-algebras, every such $f:C\to A$, every marked object $y'\in F(A')$, and every prescribed marked identification of $y'|_A$ with the evaluation at $f$, there exist a local residue-preserving $f':C\to A'$ with $qf'=f$ and a marked identification of $y'$ with the evaluation at $f'$ restricting to the prescribed identification. In the total-category formulation the last requirement is equality of the two arrows after passing to a common higher quotient level. Local means having a unique maximal ideal, Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize, and a local ring map pulls the target maximal ideal back to the source maximal ideal. All rings and test schemes lie in the same scheme universe.
